name: Refugee Status Determination (Comissão Nacional para os Refugiados)

requirements.blocker_text: Angola has a domestic refugee law -- Lei 10/15 (2015), which replaced a 1990 predecessor -- administered by the National Commission for Refugees. The legal framework theoretically covers asylum, documentation, education, family life, freedom of movement, health, housing, employment, and social protection. In practice, registration has been historically inconsistent: the government resumed refugee registration in 2023, deploying a biometric database that documented thousands of refugees and asylum seekers, but real gaps remain in freedom of movement and access to formal employment, particularly for the displaced populations concentrated in urban areas.
requirements.fix_path: Register with the National Commission for Refugees; access to services depends significantly on actual documentation being issued and processed, which this dataset's sourcing indicates has been inconsistent in practice.

evidence_required.document: National Commission for Refugees registration / biometric record

outcome.duration_length: indefinite, tied to continued registration and protection needs

sources.title: UNHCR RIMAP -- Angola's Lei 10/15 (2015), National Commission for Refugees, 2023 registration resumption and biometric database, documented implementation gaps

notes: NEW COUNTRY BUILD (Angola). STATUS: DRAFT -- sourced to UNHCR's own rights-mapping platform (tier 2), not the primary statute (Lei 10/15 could not be located and fetched directly in this build). GENUINE, HONESTLY MIXED FINDING, distinct from the cleaner positive findings for Paraguay and Bolivia earlier in this session: Angola DOES have a real, named domestic refugee law and government body (unlike Algeria, Haiti, Cuba, Afghanistan), but the source itself explicitly documents an implementation gap between the law's theoretical coverage (asylum, education, health, housing, employment, movement) and what refugees actually experience in practice, especially around freedom of movement and formal-employment access in urban areas. work_rights/study_rights set to 'restricted' rather than 'full' specifically because of this documented gap -- this dataset is treating the source's own stated implementation problems as evidence, not defaulting to the law's theoretical text. The 2023 registration resumption and biometric rollout is presented as a real, dated, positive development, not undercut by the remaining gaps -- both are true at once and both are disclosed.
